rationale: B wins because it keeps finding the trapdoor under the shiny claim: selection bias, peer-review ambiguity, free-to-teachers versus free-to-districts, and whether June 9 is really a current rollout. A has a strong opener in "Khan Academy is putting AI tutors in front of 1 million students. The study saying it works hasn't been peer-reviewed," but it decorates some angles with facts it was not given. B's "Khan Academy says its AI tutor added weeks of learning. Its own study is the first test of that claim" is cleaner: same tension, less confetti, sharper proof demands.
gaps_in_A: "While VC-backed EdTech companies charge districts" is an invented market contrast. The update says Khan is donor-funded and free to teachers; it does not say what competitors charge or who pays them.
"a body of research on productive failure and desirable difficulty argues" imports an academic frame the update did not supply. Useful if sourced, sloppy if smuggled in as fact.
"Teachers are quietly getting something else" adds mystery the facts do not earn. The update plainly says teachers get lesson-planning help; it is not a hidden second product.
The data angle asks for methodology and controls, but misses the nastiest issue in "students who used it regularly": regular users may be self-selected, not caused into gains by Khanmigo.
gaps_in_B: "Donors, not districts, are paying for the AI tutor" overcommits. The update says free to teachers and donor-funded; B wisely questions the ambiguity later, but the headline spends the money before it has the receipt.
"What one pilot district saw" needs a named district and district-level numbers. Without them, it is a good local-story shell, not yet a pitchable angle.
"defensive-comment" is an ugly category label and tilts the independent-thinking angle toward company rebuttal. Reporters want conflict and evidence, not a PR containment exercise.
B underuses the supplied teacher lesson-planning fact. A's teacher-workload angle is a real lane; B folds it into the local district story and loses a potentially distinct education-workforce pitch.
